A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MOPO research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic preference-learning experiments, phi-1.5 text-generation evaluations, hyperparameter analyses, and example outputs.

after.justification: V2 reports original synthetic experiments, text-generation evaluations across multiple models, optimizer comparisons, response-length experiments, and appendix results.

M1.justification: V2 adds MOPO-LB, an alternative optimizer using relaxed log-barrier penalties and decreasing barrier coefficients (Remark 3.2 and Appendix A.4). The original Lagrangian method remains as MOPO-Lag. The shared multi-head architecture already appeared in v1 Appendix A.6.2 and is not a new architecture.

E1.justification: The HH-RLHF and Reddit summarization datasets remain. V2 adds a response-length-constrained generation scenario, while removing the antichain and pairwise-incomparable synthetic cases from Section 4.1. Its unobserved-preference dataset D3 corresponds to v1's D5, rather than a newly added dataset.

E2.justification: PARM replaces HaM in the text-generation comparisons, while RiC, MODPO, DPO on DJ, and the three-objective RLHF comparators remain. V2 also compares MOPO-LB with MOPO-Lag. L3Ms is discussed as related work but is not directly evaluated.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands from phi-1.5 to several 7–8B models, including larger-model sensitivity and three-objective experiments. Section 4.2 changes the stated training budget from 5,000 steps/batch 4 to 10,000 steps/batch 8; however, v1's appendix already listed 10,000/8, so an actual doubling is not established. V2 also revises the beta sweep and removes tau=0.5 from the canonical synthetic sanity check.

E4.justification: V2 adds substantive tests of log-barrier versus Lagrangian optimization and response-length constraint satisfaction alongside helpfulness. The existing tau, beta, and reference-lag analyses are reworked for Llama-3.1-8B (Figures 8 and 14), rather than merely relocated. Two synthetic sanity-check cases are removed.

E5.justification: V2 explicitly reports five independent runs and one standard deviation for the text-generation results in Table 1; v1 specified this practice only for synthetic Figure 4. Conversely, v2 removes the synthetic figure's run-count and uncertainty explanation. Neither version establishes an increase in repeated-run counts.

E6.justification: V2 adds extensive multi-model reward results, MOPO-LB results, and response-length outcomes. The reported phi-1.5 three-objective MOPO tuple changes from (0.39, 0.22, 0.17) in v1 Table 1 to MOPO-Lag's (0.20, 0.10, 0.09) in v2 Table 6; the protocol reporting prevents a clean same-setting comparison. Appendix example texts are retained but reassigned from HaM/MODPO to MODPO/PARM without explanation.

T1.justification: Remark 3.2 and Appendix A.4 add the relaxed-barrier definition, limiting behavior, gradient derivation, and connection to Lagrange multipliers. V2 also corrects positive exponents to negative ones in the lower-bound proposition and proof (Propositions 3.3 and A.5.2), although practical losses in Equations 8 and 28 retain positive exponents. Earlier Pareto and threshold arguments largely remain.

C1.justification: The central preference-only constrained-alignment contribution remains. V2 expands the stated empirical scope from a 1.3B model to multi-billion-parameter models and recasts inference as avoiding user preference-vector elicitation. The abstract emphasizes empirical Pareto recovery, and the introduction removes the earlier explicit 'provably' wording.

C2.justification: V2 adds an explanation of barrier ill-conditioning and gradual constraint enforcement, and explicitly acknowledges that convergence of the practical stochastic barrier procedure is not guaranteed in this setting (Appendix A.4). The earlier limitations concerning conservative, expensive threshold initialization remain.

D1.justification: The implementation table changes hardware from an RTX 5080 with 16GB GPU memory to an A100 with 80GB, and Appendix A.7 updates training-time disclosures for the larger models. V2 explicitly describes selecting the primary-objective head at inference. Most LoRA settings, dataset/reward-model identifiers, and codebase access information are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds explicit positioning against PARM and contemporary L3Ms, together with references supporting log-barrier optimization, additional models, and length control. Appendix A.2.2 also changes citations accompanying the divergence definitions. The main critique of scalarization and preference-conditioned alternatives remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are tightened, experimental prose is reorganized, and the empirical optimization derivation moves from Section 3.1 into Appendix A.6. V2 adds an impact statement and reorganizes appendix subsections. Much of the original exposition and proof text remains intact.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column conference layout and substantially redesigns the empirical presentation. It adds colored multi-model tables, a model-alignment plot, a response-length boxplot, and a barrier plot. Bar charts replace the original sensitivity-front plots, and synthetic Figure 4 contracts from fifteen panels to six.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially addresses v1's explicit restriction to a 1.3B model through evaluations across several 7–8B models, uncertainty reporting for text-generation comparisons, and additional optimizer and constraint-satisfaction tests. These strengthen the evidence for practical applicability. Reduced synthetic coverage, unexplained example reattributions, and the incompletely propagated sign correction temper the gains, but the broader and better quantified evaluation provides a substantial net improvement.
